headline: Invivyd Outlines Accelerated Approval Submission Path with FDA for COVID-19 Antibody
summary: Invivyd reported Phase 3 LIBERTY trial data for VYD2311, showing strong safety and enhanced COVID-19 antibody levels.
content_html:
Invivyd Inc. (NASDAQ:IVVD) on Tuesday announced topline results from its Phase 3 LIBERTY study of its investigational COVID-19 monoclonal antibody candidate.

The study demonstrated that VYD2311 met primary and key secondary safety endpoints while enhancing antibody titers when combined with an mRNA vaccine.

Read Also: Invivyd Stock Surges As FDA Alignment Boosts COVID-19 Program

Safety And Tolerability Outcomes

The double-blind study evaluated 210 healthy adults aged 18 to 49 across three treatment arms: VYD2311 alone, the Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE)/BioNTech SE (NASDAQ:BNTX) Comirnaty mRNA vaccine alone, or a combination of both treatments.

Participants receiving VYD2311 alone reported a lower incidence of short-term treatment-emergent adverse events over six days at 56.5%, compared to 91.4% in the mRNA vaccine group.

Over the full 56 days, VYD2311 maintained favorable tolerability with a 60.9% adverse event rate versus 91.4% for the vaccine alone.

Short-term systemic adverse events occurred in 44.1% of participants receiving VYD2311 and 50.0% receiving the combination therapy, demonstrating statistically significant reductions compared to 68.1% for the mRNA vaccine alone.

Investigators observed no adverse events exceeding Grade 2 and recorded zero instances of hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis across all treatment groups.

Antibody Titers And Regulatory Strategy

The trial evaluated potential immunologic interference by measuring vaccine-induced neutralizing antiviral titers.

Combining VYD2311 with the mRNA vaccine increased neutralizing titers by approximately 2.5 times compared to the vaccine alone over 56 days.

When researchers removed VYD2311 from combination samples, neutralizing titers remained identical to the standalone vaccine arm, confirming an absence of immunologic interference.

Pharmacokinetic results met company expectations and target profiles under evaluation in the companion DECLARATION trial.

These comparative analyses suggest concomitant administration may improve vaccine safety while expanding neutralizing antiviral coverage.

Following a September Type C meeting and ongoing discussions with U.S. Food and Drug Administration leadership, the company intends to submit a Biologics License Application under the Accelerated Approval Program.

Invivyd will base the application on LIBERTY and DECLARATION data, while continuing post-approval clinical event collection in a randomized confirmatory cohort to evaluate efficacy.

headline: Pfizer Says Eczema Drug Shows Significant Skin Clearance
summary: Pfizer reports positive Phase 2 trial results for tilrekimig in treating moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis at the EADV Congress.
content_html:
Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) on Thursday presented detailed Phase 2 results for tilrekimig (PF-07275315) in adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.

The ongoing trial met its primary endpoint, showing a statistically significant increase in participants achieving EASI-75 at Week 16 across all evaluated doses compared to placebo.

Strong Efficacy Across Phase 2 Trial Stages

The trial evaluated biologic-naïve adult patients across two distinct stages. Stage 1 tested subcutaneous tilrekimig at 450 mg every two weeks, where 62.5% of patients achieved EASI-75 compared to 19.9% in the placebo group.

Stage 2 evaluated monthly dosing options of 400 mg, 200 mg, or 50 mg. In these monthly cohorts, 58.5%, 61.0%, and 47.8% of patients reached EASI-75, representing absolute improvements of 49.4%, 51.9%, and 38.7% over the 9.1% placebo rate.

Read Also: Trump's Drug Price Achievements Questioned Following Separate Most Favored Nation Contract Disclosures with Lilly, Pfizer

Key secondary endpoints measuring clear or almost clear skin (vIGA 0/1) showed 30.3% achievement in Stage 1 versus 11.8% for placebo.

In Stage 2, 26% to 27% of patients across monthly cohorts reached vIGA 0/1, compared to 0% in the placebo group.

An exploratory analysis also demonstrated significant itch reduction, as 42.5% of patients in the 400 mg monthly group and 50.8% in the 200 mg group achieved a 4-point or greater improvement in peak pruritus scores versus 7.2% on placebo.

Novel Mechanism And Safety Results

Tilrekimig is a potential first-in-class trispecific antibody engineered to inhibit type 2 inflammation by targeting IL-4, IL-13, and TSLP. Concurrently blocking TSLP and its downstream effectors provides broader cytokine pathway coverage.

An extended half-life of approximately 37 days supports convenient monthly dosing.

The antibody was well-tolerated with no dose-dependent safety signals.

summary: Vaxcyte announced positive Phase 3 OPUS-1 trial results for its VAX-31 vaccine candidate, setting the stage for an FDA BLA filing.
content_html:
Vaxcyte Inc. (NASDAQ:PCVX) stock is surging on Monday on positive topline results from its pivotal Phase 3 OPUS-1 trial evaluating VAX-31, an investigational 31-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine.

The trial assessed the safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of the candidate in adults to prevent invasive pneumococcal disease and pneumococcal pneumonia.

These trial findings will form the foundation for an upcoming Biologics License Application submission to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Primary Immunogenicity Endpoints Met

In the OPUS-1 trial, VAX-31 achieved all prespecified co-primary immunogenicity endpoints in participants aged 50 and older.

The vaccine candidate met noninferiority criteria across all 28 serotypes shared with existing vaccines Pfizer Inc.’s (NYSE:PFE) Prevnar 20 (PCV20) and/or Merck & Co Inc.’s (NYSE:MRK) Capvaxive (PCV21).

Specifically, VAX-31 matched noninferiority standards for 11 serotypes common to both PCV20 and PCV21 based on opsonophagocytic activity geometric mean ratios.

Furthermore, the candidate met noninferiority benchmarks for nine serotypes shared exclusively with PCV20 and eight serotypes shared solely with PCV21.

Read Also: Pfizer Expands Pneumococcal Vaccine Push With New Programs

For the three unique serotypes alongside the cross-reactive serotype 20B, VAX-31 demonstrated superiority over the comparative vaccines.

Strong Immunobridging And Safety Profile

The trial also evaluated immunobridging in adults aged 18 to 49 compared to adults aged 50 to 64. VAX-31 met noninferiority criteria across all 321 serotype comparisons within this group.

Individual comparator analyses showed VAX-31 met noninferiority for 20 of 20 serotypes shared with PCV20 and 17 of 19 shared with PCV21, with serotypes 3 and 12F meeting historical threshold limits.

Safety evaluations confirmed that VAX-31 showed strong tolerability with a profile comparable to PCV20 and PCV21 across all tested age groups.

Solicited local and systemic reactions remained mostly mild-to-moderate, with most resolving within 48 hours.

Researchers recorded no vaccine-related serious adverse events or trial discontinuations due to adverse effects.

Future Clinical Pipeline Milestones

Looking ahead, the company plans to report data from the OPUS-2 and OPUS-3 adult Phase 3 trials in the first half of 2027.

Additionally, management expects Phase 2 trial results for infant indications by the end of the first half of 2027.

A legal filing in Florida accuses pharmaceutical giant Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) and Chairman and CEO Albert Bourla of deceiving consumers by concealing critical safety risks and unverified transmission claims.

Who is Suing?

The lawsuit was filed by the Office of the Attorney General of the State of Florida (Department of Legal Affairs), on behalf of the State of Florida, led by Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier.

It alleges that Pfizer violated the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act by misleading the public, hiding internal safety data, and disparaging concerned citizens.

Benzinga has reached out to Pfizer for comments and will update the story upon receiving their stance.

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier has opposed the corporate marketing and forced mandates of the COVID-19 vaccine, publicly accusing drug manufacturers of concealing serious health risks.

Aggressive Marketing Campaign Drives Massive Revenue

According to the court document, Pfizer spent more than $10 billion on advertising from 2020 to 2023 to build consumer demand for its novel mRNA COVID-19 vaccine.

This extensive marketing push successfully generated over $80 billion in vaccine sales for the company. During this same period, Bourla earned nearly $102 million in compensation, supplemented by stock profits and book sales.

To secure these windfall profits, Pfizer executives conducted media appearances assuring Florida residents the vaccine was completely safe. Bourla publicly declared that the company had not observed a single safety signal.

Furthermore, Pfizer pressured consumers by asserting that mass vaccination was a moral duty required to prevent transmitting the virus to loved ones.

Complaint Alleges Concealed Safety Risks And Unverified Claims

However, the state lawsuit asserts Pfizer possessed internal data reflecting serious safety risks that were hidden from the public. These included links to myocarditis and pericarditis in minors, strokes, and elderly fatalities.

The complaint also highlights concerns over adverse events for pregnant women, including miscarriages, which were discussed among Anthony Fauci, Surgeon General Vivek Murthy, and CDC Director Rochelle Walensky.

The filing further claims Pfizer had never tested the vaccine’s effect on transmission when making those moral appeals to consumers.

Instead of offering full public transparency, Pfizer actively worked to quash opposition by branding skeptics as criminals, leveraging deceptive practices to protect corporate revenues at the expense of Florida consumers making sensitive medical choices.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Wednesday approved Pfizer Inc.’s (NYSE:PFE) TUKYSA (tucatinib) in combination with trastuzumab and pertuzumab.

This regimen serves as a maintenance therapy for adults battling unresectable locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer following their initial induction treatment.

This regulatory decision stems from the robust HER2CLIMB-05 Phase 3 trial. Patients receiving the TUKYSA combination experienced a 35.9% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death compared to those taking a placebo alongside trastuzumab and pertuzumab.

The median progression-free survival reached 24.9 months for the TUKYSA arm, outperforming the 16.3 months observed in the placebo group. This provides patients with an additional 8.6 months of life without their cancer advancing.

Expanding Front-Line Treatment Options

TUKYSA already holds a Category 1 designation from the National Comprehensive Cancer Network as a second-line or later therapy for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer in the U.S.

This new approval elevates the drug to the front-line setting. It provides a valuable chemotherapy-free maintenance alternative, helping physicians tailor individual treatment strategies while successfully delaying disease progression.

headline: Pharma Lobby Sues Trump Administration Over Medicare Drug Pricing Rule, Calls It ‘Unlawful Overreach’ — ‘The Results Are Preordained’
summary: PhRMA sued the Trump administration over its Medicare drug pricing rule, arguing CMS exceeded its authority under federal law.
content_html:
The pharmaceutical industry’s top lobby group Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA) sued the Trump administration on Wednesday to invalidate its “most-favored-nation” drug pricing rule for Medicare, arguing the rule is illegal government overreach.

The suit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia. Defendants include Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz and Abe Sutton, who directs the CMS innovation center.

What the GLOBE Rule Does

The GLOBE rule, finalized last week, would use drug prices in economically comparable countries to calculate Medicare Part B rebates for certain drugs, effectively lowering the amount Medicare pays for eligible drugs.

The rule is expected to have limited reach. CMS plans to waive it for manufacturers that signed voluntary pricing deals with the White House.

Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE), Eli Lilly and Co. (NYSE:LLY) and Novo Nordisk A/S (NYSE:NVO) are among more than two dozen drugmakers with Trump-signed deals.

PhRMA Says CMS Overstepped Its Authority

In the final rule, HHS cut its projected Medicare Part B net spending savings to $440 million over seven years, a 96% drop from the $11.9 billion in the proposed rule.

PhRMA argues CMS is stretching Section 1115A of the Social Security Act, which lets it test payment models, to rewrite Medicare drug pricing without Congress. GLOBE is not a true test, the complaint says, because “the results are preordained.” It adds that Congress, “unlike CMS, has decided that [most-favored-nation]-based price controls do not serve the national interest.”

Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to Benzinga‘s request for comment.

content_html:
A nationwide initiative to accelerate personalized cancer vaccine development is drawing fresh investor interest in vaccine makers, sending several biotechnology and pharmaceutical stocks higher Friday.

Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA), Novavax, Inc. (NASDAQ:NVAX), BioNTech SE (NASDAQ:BNTX), Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE), Merck & Co., Inc. (NYSE:MRK) and Vaxcyte, Inc. (NASDAQ:PCVX) traded higher.

The rally followed a New York Times report detailing a new public-private partnership involving the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to speed up cancer vaccine research.

NIH Cancer Vaccine Initiative Targets December Launch

The initiative will bring together the NIH, the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health, researchers, pharmaceutical companies, biotech firms, advocacy groups and patients.

The program is expected to launch in December, according to the New York Times.

Initially, researchers will focus on pancreatic, liver and colorectal cancers, along with certain childhood tumors.

Unlike traditional vaccines that prevent infections, personalized cancer vaccines aim to help the immune system identify and attack existing cancer cells.

Many experimental treatments use messenger RNA, or mRNA, technology to target abnormal proteins unique to a patient’s tumor.

Stacey Adam, a senior clinical officer at the NIH foundation, said the initiative aims to replicate the collaboration that accelerated COVID-19 vaccine development.

Moderna, BioNTech Could Benefit From Cancer Vaccine Push

The initiative could strengthen research efforts in a field where Moderna and BioNTech already have significant clinical programs.

In August, Moderna and Merck reported positive Phase 3 results for their personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, intismeran autogene, combined with Keytruda.

Meanwhile, BioNTech is advancing several clinical-stage cancer therapies, including BNT113 for HPV-positive tumors, BNT116 for lung cancer and autogene cevumeran (BNT122), developed with Genentech.

headline: Swiss Pharma Giant Roche Suspends German Capital Commitments Amid Dispute Over Drug Discounts
summary: Roche halts German investments as chief Daniel Steiners warns Berlin that statutory drug rebates shatter trust in the market.
content_html:
Roche Holdings AG (OTC:RHHBY) Germany chief Daniel Steiners announced that the Swiss pharmaceutical giant has put all future investment decisions in Germany on hold.

The Swiss drug maker argues that recent government healthcare austerity requirements have shattered corporate trust and undermined long-term planning for the pharmaceutical sector.

Mandatory Rebates Erode Industry Confidence

Steiners voiced sharp opposition to the GKV Contribution Rate Stabilization Act, which increases statutory manufacturer discounts on patent-protected drugs from 7% to 15.5% starting in January 2027.

Read Also: Roche Secures FDA Approval for First At-Home Thyroid Eye Disease Therapy

While Germany’s health ministry expects the measure to save health insurers around 12 billion euros by 2030 to help bridge an estimated 19 billion euros financing shortfall, Steiners warned that such short-term austerity ignores structural financing issues and risks driving research and production abroad.

Steiners also dismissed Berlin’s proposed location clause—which offers partial rebate relief to companies with extensive domestic research and manufacturing—as inadequate.

He insisted that piecemeal adjustments cannot replace a comprehensive industrial strategy, contrasting Germany’s tightening regulatory climate with the U.S., where supportive policies and infrastructure assistance actively attract life sciences capital.

Setback For Merz’s Economic Pitch

The investment freeze delivers a direct blow to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who is actively pitching the country to global executives at a Berlin investor summit.

Financial Times noted in August that Roche is not alone in pulling back; U.S.-based drugmaker Eli Lilly and Co. (NYSE:LLY) recently halved a planned 2.3 billion euros manufacturing investment, while Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) placed its domestic allocations under review and Boehringer Ingelheim scrapped a 900 million euros expenditure.

Statutory health insurance officials strongly defended the government’s reforms. Stefanie Stoff-Ahnis, deputy chairwoman of the GKV association, maintained that pharmaceutical companies continue to enjoy substantial profits in Germany, cautioning that higher drug prices would destabilize recently balanced insurance finances without offering tangible benefits to patients.

Roche employs around 18,600 people in Germany and has poured approximately 3.8 billion euros into expanding its domestic sites since 2020.

A company spokeswoman told FT that the freeze applies exclusively to unapproved future projects, ensuring that ongoing construction at its Penzberg biotechnology hub and current workforce headcounts remain secure for now.

Roche Expands China-Based Partnership

On the other hand, on Monday, Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. announced a second collaboration with Roche in the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) field.

The strategic collaboration spans a broad portfolio of ADC programs, comprising two preclinical Hansoh ADC programs and multiple ADC programs based on Roche-proposed targets powered by Hansoh’s proprietary ADC technology platform.

Under the collaboration agreement, Hansoh will lead the early development of the programs up to the completion of global PhaseⅠa clinical trials.

Roche will be responsible for further developing the programs worldwide (excluding the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan). Hansoh will retain all rights to develop, register and commercialize the programs within the Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan.

Hansoh will receive an upfront payment of $400 million as well as a first anniversary payment of $110 million, and will be eligible to receive potentially more than $15 billion in milestone payments.

Strong Progression-Free Survival Results

The study achieved its primary endpoint of progression-free survival at a pre-specified interim efficacy analysis.

Elrexfio demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction in the risk of disease progression or death compared to three standard-of-care regimens selected by investigators.

More than 75% of patients receiving Elrexfio avoided disease progression or death at the time of analysis, showing an estimated 68% progression-free survival rate at 18 months.

Secondary endpoint data for overall survival remain immature, and researchers will continue monitoring patients until the next scheduled analysis.

ELREXFIO demonstrated a safety profile consistent with its known characteristics, generating no new safety signals.

Early infection prophylaxis measures helped mitigate infection risks. Grade 3 or higher infections developed in 27.5% of patients receiving Elrexfio versus 18.1% on investigator’s choice, while Grade 5 infections occurred in 0.8% of Elrexfio patients compared to 1.6% in the control group.

headline: How To Earn $500 A Month From Pfizer Stock Ahead Of Q3 Earnings
summary: Pfizer expects Q3 EPS of 73¢ and revenue of $15.88B; its 5.64% dividend yield requires ~$106,454 to generate $500 monthly.
content_html:
Pfizer Inc (NYSE:PFE) investors may be eyeing potential gains from the company’s dividends ahead of its third-quarter report on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

Currently, Pfizer has an annual dividend yield of 5.64%, with a quarterly dividend of 43 cents per share ($1.72 a year). So, how can investors exploit its dividend yield to pocket a regular $500 monthly?

To earn $500 per month or $6,000 annually from dividends alone, you would need an investment of about $106,454 or around 3,488 shares. For a more modest $100 per month or $1,200 per year, you would need $21,303 or around 698 shares.

To Calculate

Divide the desired annual income ($6,000 or $1,200) by the dividend ($1.72 in this case). So, $6,000 / $1.72 = 3,488 shares ($500 per month), and $1,200 / $1.72 = 698 shares ($100 per month).

Note that dividend yield can change on a rolling basis, as dividend payments and stock prices both fluctuate over time.

How It Works

The dividend yield is computed by dividing the annual dividend payment by the stock’s current price.

For example, if a stock pays an annual dividend of $2 and trades at $50, the dividend yield is 4% ($2/$50). However, if the stock price increases to $60, the dividend yield drops to 3.33% ($2/$60). Conversely, if the stock price falls to $40, the dividend yield rises to 5% ($2/$40).

Similarly, changes in dividend payments can affect yield. If a company increases its dividend, the yield will also increase, provided the stock price stays the same. Conversely, if the dividend payment decreases, the yield will too.

content_html:

U.S. stocks settled mixed on Monday, with the Nasdaq Composite falling more than 1% during the session amid a decline in tech stocks. Shares of Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) each fell over 1% on Monday.

Most sectors on the S&P 500 closed on a positive note, with consumer discretionary, materials and financial stocks recording the biggest gains on Monday. However, energy and information technology stocks were among the worst performers.

The Dow Jones closed higher by around 214 points to 51,983.98 on Monday. The S&P 500 fell 0.51% to 7,541.40, while the Nasdaq Composite tumbled 1.07% at 25,164.36 during Monday’s session.

Investors are awaiting earnings results from Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE), Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. (NASDAQ:KDP) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) today.

What is CNN Business Fear & Greed Index?

At a current reading of 23, the index moved to the “Extreme Fear” zone on Monday, versus a prior reading of 26.

The Fear & Greed Index is a measure of the current market sentiment. It is based on the premise that higher fear exerts pressure on stock prices, while higher greed has the opposite effect. The index is calculated based on seven equal-weighted indicators. The index ranges from 0 to 100, where 0 represents maximum fear and 100 signals maximum greediness.

headline: Non-COVID Portfolio Steps Up: Pfizer Outpaces Consensus and Hikes Guidance
summary: Pfizer beats Q3 revenue and profit forecasts on oncology and non-COVID drug growth, raising its full-year 2026 sales and EPS outlook.
content_html:
Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) on Tuesday reported third-quarter sales of $16.58 billion, beating the consensus of $15.87 billion.

The company said revenues came in ahead of expectations, with strong 7% operational revenue growth in non-COVID products, driven by key brands in the U.S. and select international markets, offset by lower revenues from COVID-19 products.

Pfizer’s adjusted earnings came in at 87 cents per share, beating the consensus of 72 cents.

Revenue Drivers and Non-COVID Portfolio Performance

Total revenue dipped slightly from a year earlier. The operational decrease was driven by lower revenues from COVID-19 products and the Prevnar family, largely offset by higher revenues for Eliquis, Padcev, the Vyndaqel family, Nurtec and Lorbrena.

Excluding contributions from Comirnaty and Paxlovid, revenues for the third quarter grew 7% operationally.

Launched and acquired products contributed $3.8 billion in revenues and grew 32% operationally.

Read Also: Florida Attorney General Sues Pfizer for 'Misleading' COVID-19 Vaccine Safety Claims

Key Drug Sales: Oncology Gains Offset Vaccine Declines

Eliquis (a blood thinner) sales were up 25% to $2.52 billion. Padcev (a cancer drug) sales jumped 55% to $720 million.

Vyndaqel family sales increased 12% to $1.77 billion. Paxlovid sales fell 63% to $449 million, and Comirnaty revenues were $808 million, down 29%.

Prevnar family sales were down 10% to $1.56 billion.

Long-Term Outlook and Pipeline Developments

In earnings prepared remarks, Chairman and CEO Albert Bourla said, “I’m confident Pfizer is well positioned for growth toward the end of the decade and for long-term shareholder value creation. We have line of sight to our aim of delivering a risk-adjusted high-single-digit revenue CAGR from year-end 2028 through year-end 2033.”

Bourla also said, “Our obesity program continued to advance, and recent milestones in oncology, immunology and vaccines further demonstrate the potential of our pipeline. With a robust slate of expected catalysts ahead, I believe we’re well positioned to deliver meaningful new medicines for patients and lasting value in the years ahead.”

Upgraded Full-Year 2026 Guidance

Pfizer raised its fiscal 2026 sales guidance to $62 billion to $64 billion, from $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion, compared with the consensus of $62.17 billion.

The U.S. drug giant raised its 2026 adjusted earnings guidance to $2.95 to $3.05 per share, from $2.80 to $3.00 per share, versus the consensus of $2.96.

Summary

The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $62-$64 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $2.95-$3.05, citing strong performance and confidence in executing its strategy.

Pfizer’s focus on cost discipline is expected to yield $7.2 billion in net savings by the end of 2026, with an additional $2.5 billion anticipated in savings from 2027-2029.

The company is optimistic about potential high single-digit revenue CAGR from 2028-2033, driven by pipeline products and margin expansion through cost realignment initiatives.

CEO Albert Bourla expressed confidence in the company’s strategic direction and long-term growth prospects, highlighting the importance of pipeline execution and strong commercial capabilities.

OPERATOR

Good day everyone, and welcome to Pfizer’s third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. Today’s call is being recorded. At this time, I would like to turn the call over to Francesca DiMartino, Chief Investor Relations Officer and Senior Vice President. Please go ahead, ma’am.

Good morning and welcome to Pfizer’s earnings call. I’m Francesca DiMartino, Chief Investor Relations Officer. On behalf of the Pfizer team, thank you for joining us. This call is being made available via audio webcast. Earlier this morning we released our results for the third quarter 2026 via a press release that is available on our website at pfizer.com. I’m joined today by Dr. Albert Bourla, our chairman and CEO, Cecile Gagan, our CFO, and Chris Boshoff, our Chief Scientific Officer.

After their prepared remarks, we will open the call for questions. Members of our leadership team will be available for the Q&A session. Before we get started, I want to remind you that we will be making forward-looking statements and discussing certain non-GAAP financial measures. I encourage you to read the disclaimers in our slide presentation, the press release we issued this morning, and the disclosures in our SEC filings, which are all available on the IR website on pfizer.com. Forward-looking statements on the call are subject to substantial risks and uncertainty, speak only as of the call’s original date, and we undertake no obligation to update or revise any of the statements.

With that, I will turn the call over to Albert.

Albert Bourla (Chairman of the Board)

Thank you, Francesca. Good morning everyone, and thank you for joining our call. I’m pleased with another strong quarter for Pfizer. Our excellent commercial execution, including 32% operational revenue growth in the quarter for our launched and acquired products, shows the underlying strength of our business. Financial discipline and ongoing productivity improvement are driving efficiency and contributing favorably toward our margins. And with continued progress of our high-value R&D programs, we believe that we are on a pathway to the next stage of meaningful growth.

Before going further, I want to welcome Cecile Gagan as our Chief Financial Officer. Cecile brings more than 25 years of finance leadership and the proven ability to deliver new sources of growth. She stood out in a global search for her expertise, her deep knowledge of Pfizer and our industry, and a strategic vision that I believe will help Pfizer unlock sustained long-term value for patients and shareholders. I’m looking forward to Cecile’s partnership, and I’m confident she will help us execute with the discipline and ambition this next chapter requires.

Now let me cover several highlights of our progress in this quarter. As you know, over the last few years we have invested close to $80 billion in transactions that have equipped us with key products contributing to current commercial momentum and platforms with transformative potential. About 80% of this investment was for Seagen, Arena, and Biohaven, and we are making good progress in maximizing the value of each one. We are pleased with the overall performance of our acquired products, which grew 37% operationally in this quarter.

Our legacy Seagen portfolio grew 39% year over year in the U.S. in the quarter, driven by the strong performance of Padcev. Bringing Seagen medicines together with the strength and reach of our commercial organization has deepened our presence in the oncology community. We now offer physicians and care teams a broader set of options and more expertise, helping patients and driving growth for Pfizer. Seagen did more than strengthen our commercial position.

It also expanded our ability to discover oncology breakthroughs, doubling the size of our early-stage pipeline at the time we closed the acquisition. In our late-stage development programs, we are advancing potential antibody-drug conjugates that could bring meaningful improvements for patients with cancer. I’m pleased with the pace of progress over the past year with our expansive clinical development program across our obesity portfolio. We plan to advance 10 active and planned Phase 3 trials in 2026, including one evaluating a switch from approved weekly therapies to our investigational monthly GLP-1 peptide, barobenatide. We have made significant progress with enrollment across our pivotal barobenatide program as well as our amylin combination program, where our Phase 2b study is now fully enrolled.

We are working toward the first in a series of potential approvals for barobenatide in 2028, with planning of our go-to-market strategy well underway. Biohaven also has been a strategically important addition for Pfizer. In the quarter, Nurtec grew by 33% operationally, driven by underlying demand and excellent commercial execution. We see real opportunity to help patients with migraine and for the oral CGRP class to be a key growth driver even as we manage market dynamics in a competitive field. We are leading the oral class in the U.S. and are working to extend that position internationally. We are seeing international growth as more patients can now get this treatment in key countries including the UK, Italy, and Japan.

We are also encouraged by strong adoption when we are able to expand access. 2026 execution in R&D has been strong, and we continue to prioritize the highest-value opportunities for patients and future growth across our four therapeutic focus areas. Our excellent progress showcases our momentum in advancing our strategy. In recent months we achieved two key regulatory decisions, one key pivotal readout, and eight key pivotal study starts alongside strong data we presented at several recent medical congresses. We are excited by the pipeline opportunities in areas of strategic focus and commercial strength.

This includes late-stage programs across tumor types in oncology including multiple myeloma, breast cancer, and lung cancer, within inflammation and immunology, and of course in pneumococcal vaccines. Chris will share more detail about our recent advancement in the recent months. Our pipeline strategy is grounded in disciplined prioritization and accelerated execution, and we are confident that we are advancing our most significant opportunities for future patient impact and growth.

Today we are raising our guidance for full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted earnings per share. This reflects our strong performance through the third quarter and confidence in our ability to execute our strategy, along with our financial discipline and the progress we continue to make with our R&D pipeline. We believe Pfizer is well positioned to drive growth towards the end of the decade and create sustained value for patients and shareholders over the long term.

We have deployed AI in our business with the goal of improving efficiency in manufacturing and sharpening how we engage physicians and patients in R&D. We are working to accelerate innovation with faster target validation and better molecule and biomarker selection. The recent launch of Genesys, a new pharmacovigilance platform, shows our commitment to harnessing advanced AI and intelligent automation for global safety monitoring. This typically involves a lengthy manual process for more than 600 products in over 120 countries.

Genesys takes on the administrative burden so our safety scientists can spend their time where it matters most: assessing causality, detecting safety signals, and protecting patients. With that, I will turn it over to Cecile.

Chris Boshoff (Chief Scientific Officer and President, Research & Development)

Thanks, Cecile. Across our four therapeutic areas, we made strong progress last quarter. I’ll provide color on recent developments for some of these programs, starting with Elrexfio, our internally discovered BCMA bispecific, which has now delivered two positive Phase 3 readouts in double-class–exposed multiple myeloma, most recently in MM32. Elrexfio monotherapy demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival versus investigator’s choice of three established standard-of-care regimens.

A key limitation of this class is safety and tolerability, with CDK6 inhibition being a key contributor to adverse events. We designed atirmociclib to maximize efficacy through greater CDK4 inhibition while improving tolerability by minimizing CDK6 engagement. Atirmociclib is 33 times more selective for CDK4 versus CDK6, comparing favorably versus the standard of care. Here are two data sets fueling enthusiasm for atirmociclib. Any-grade diarrhea was lower than with abemaciclib and comparable to palbociclib and ribociclib. So we are learning a lot and we are very happy that we are entering this market because I think it is cut for our capabilities. With that I will ask Chris to comment on the Lyme disease.

Chris Boshoff (Chief Scientific Officer and President, Research & Development)

Thank you for the question. We all know Lyme disease incidence is now—the burden of the disease is increasing globally. The EMA has validated the MAA for Pfizer and Valneva’s Lyme disease vaccine candidate. With the validation, the CHMP will now begin its assessment of the MAA and the CHMP is expected to issue an opinion on marketing authorization 2027. We’ve also now filed in Canada and we continue our discussions with the FDA and should provide an update regarding this in Q4 this year.

Thank you.

Albert Bourla (Chairman of the Board)

Alexander, any comments here?

Alexandre de Germay (Chief International Commercial Officer)

Yeah, no, I think it’s a very exciting opportunity. Just to remind you that we already have an FSME franchise in Europe and we know how to activate tick-borne populations in those endemic areas because we have a salesforce, we have a commercial play with pharmacies, and so we are very excited with the opportunity. The level of awareness of the population is significantly higher than what we have in FSME. So as we have built these muscles commercially, once we have the approval, we’re very much looking forward for the opportunity to commercialize this vaccine.

Albert Bourla (Chairman of the Board)

Yeah. And the awareness of the disease, of course, in the US is skyrocketing right now because we do have an increase of severity and incidence. So we are looking forward to concluding the discussion with FDA and submitting our file. Let’s go to the next question please.

OPERATOR

Our next question comes from Michael Yee with UBS. Please go ahead.

Michael Yee (Analyst)

Great, thanks. Maybe two quick pipeline questions for Chris on MedPro. You guys continue to be pretty bullish. I know there was a formulation change to lower the Cmax and improve the tolerability. Maybe you could comment on how you feel about dropouts and the change in formulation to drive your effect and then on to recommend your tri-specific. Again, something you’re pretty bullish on is, can you just comment on neutralizing antibodies or ADAs, things that can be tricky for bispecifics and trispecifics, and how you feel about that.

Thank you.

Chris Boshoff (Chief Scientific Officer and President, Research & Development)

Thank you very much. On the first question on meprometostat, as you pointed out, we did, for the Phase 3 study, adapt to have a more tolerable dose with food where we decrease the Cmax but see similar AUC to what we’ve seen in Phase 1. So we’re very confident in the PK data and the dose that was selected for the Phase 3 study. Regarding tilrigamic, we have not seen functional neutralizing antibodies or functional ADAs thus far. You’re absolutely correct, for any bispecific or trispecific that’s a long-term risk, but so far we haven’t seen anything impacting efficacy and, in fact, longer-term follow-up on the studies we previously demonstrated or showed show us that we do not have an impact on efficacy. So, so far so good with

Albert Bourla (Chairman of the Board)

Very good. Let’s keep it that way if you can, please. Next question, please.

OPERATOR

Our final question today comes from Asad Haider with Goldman Sachs. Your line is now open.

Asad Haider (Analyst)

Great. Thanks for taking the question and congrats on the quarter, Cecile, and also many congrats and best of luck to you. A couple for you. First, just on 2027. Appreciate the context provided earlier on price dynamics with respect to IRA and 340B, et cetera, but just any additional high-level qualitative framing on other pushes and pulls next year to be aware of ahead of formal guidance. And how should we be thinking about your guidance philosophy relative to Dave’s broadly speaking?

And then looking out longer term, you are reiterating line of sight to high single-digit revenue CAGR towards the end of the decade off of a 2028 base, as well as citing operating leverage and margin expansion given the cost realignment initiatives. But consensus numbers are not really modeling that. There does seem to be a disconnect on both revenue and the earnings lines versus your own expectations. So as you examined street forecasts, what are the key assumptions that you think are getting most mismodeled in the P&L relative to your own internal expectations as you look out towards that period?

Thank you.

Albert Bourla (Chairman of the Board)

Cecile. Please make the comments on both.

Cecile

So thanks, Asad, for your question and also for your good wishes. So we’ll provide 2027 guidance around middle of December like we did last year. So I will only for now provide high-level key drivers that we are seeing in 2027. One, obviously the LOE impact not only in the U.S. with Ibrance and Xtandi and some other products, but also in international where we are seeing Eliquis being LOE at the end of 2026. The other thing that I would say is obviously offsetting that is the ramp-up and the launch of our—the ramp-up of our launched and acquired portfolio which, again, as you have seen, is having a very strong performance and NTL opportunity for growth. And then obviously pricing, including MF and IRA, which we will reflect in our guidance.

And then on our cost initiative program that will allow us to continue to, one, invest towards the growth opportunities, the growth drivers that we have on the SINA marketing and commercial space, and then increase the productivity and the growth savings both on the commercial spend and as well on the general and administrative spend. So that’s kind of like the key trends for 2027. But again, more to come as we release guidance later in the year.

As it relates to our high single-digit growth aspiration versus the street, if you look at where that difference is coming from, it’s not really coming from one place or one front product. And so is our growth trajectory either. So what we are seeing as a building block for our growth trajectory—obviously one is the continued growth of our new and acquired product. Not only because the market is still growing, our penetration is still increasing, but also on top of it, we are bringing new indications onto those products in order to be able to continue to address more patient and grow our presence on the market.

The second thing is on the pipeline. So while there are some obvious products that are making a key difference, in our view, versus the street view—obesity being one, some of the oncology products being one—what I will say is our growth trajectory doesn’t rely on one single product or one single therapeutic area. We have a broad portfolio of product, several Phase 3 ongoing as well as upcoming catalysts over the 18 to 24 months, which should give confidence to the outside world also to see the opportunity that we are having in bringing breakthroughs to patients in significant areas of unmet need.

Albert Bourla (Chairman of the Board)

Thank you, Cecile. And I would add that me as a CEO, when I see the difference between our internal projections and the street projections, that of course creates to me the urgency to check our assumptions to make sure that, in light of different opinions from the analysts, we are correct or not. So we have done that repeatedly and we came to the conclusion that we tell you that we expect to have a high single digit from ’28 to ’33 and we know very well where are the discrepancies between the products.

And as Cecile said, they are not only on the pipeline, which many analysts do not cover. So you have the phenomenon that from 12–13 analysts that are forming the overall performance of 2031, for some products only five analysts have this one and the others they don’t. So this is something that is expected in pipeline, but we see also very big discrepancies in already launched new products—that there’s a big difference. I will mention two as just examples that I think people need to reevaluate their assessment. One, it is regarding Nurtec, that we are already close to $2 billion this way if you annualize it, and the street has us almost two and a half by year 2030. So I think there is a discrepancy there. I will also mention another example of the Rex field, where for a competing product the street is forecasting $5 billion and for us $600 million. We aspire to present a profile that is very similar in efficacy and better in tolerability and in side effects.

Now, remains to be proven. But I don’t think the $600 million vis-à-vis $5 billion, it is justifiable even with the current information. So I think that as more information is coming for our pipeline and readouts, I think as more information is coming for the performance actually of the new products—and that includes new launches and acquired products—I think the street probably will start adjusting their numbers and there will be convergence mostly. But with that I think that we come to the end of our call. I want to say that I’m very proud of our performance through the third quarter and the execution, and my thanks goes to my Pfizer colleagues.

As I visit with our people—and I do that in our labs and in manufacturing sites and in markets across the world—I see a team with tremendous talent, dedication, striving for breakthroughs that change patients’ lives. We look forward to sharing additional updates about our progress. And thank you for joining our company call today, and thank you for your interest in Pfizer.

headline: Nasdaq Surges 1%; Pfizer Posts Upbeat Q3 Earnings
summary: U.S. stocks were mixed as Nasdaq gained 1%; Pfizer beat Q3 estimates and raised 2026 guidance, while oil, gold and European shares fell.
content_html:
U.S. stocks traded mixed midway through trading, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining around 1% on Tuesday.

The Dow traded down 0.46% to 51,744.97 while the NASDAQ climbed 1.01% to 25,419.67. The S&P 500 also rose, gaining, 0.49% to 7,578.55.

Leading and Lagging Sectors

Information technology shares jumped by 1.6% on Tuesday.

In trading on Tuesday, materials stocks fell by 1.6%.

Top Headline

Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) on Tuesday reported upbeat results for the third quarter.

The company posted third-quarter sales of $16.58 billion, beating the consensus of $15.87 billion. Pfizer’s adjusted earnings came in at 87 cents per share, beating the consensus of 72 cents.

Pfizer raised its fiscal 2026 sales guidance to $62 billion to $64 billion, from $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion, compared with the consensus of $62.17 billion. The U.S. drug giant raised its 2026 adjusted earnings guidance to $2.95 to $3.05 per share, from $2.80 to $3.00 per share, versus the consensus of $2.96.

Equities Trading UP
           

  • Ibotta Inc (NYSE:IBTA) shares shot up 28% to $63.85 after the company reported better-than-expected third-quarter financial results and issued fourth-quarter sales guidance above estimates.
  • Shares of Aehr Test Systems (NASDAQ:AEHR) got a boost, surging 23% to $63.20 after the company reported better-than-expected first-quarter financial results and raised its FY27 sales guidance above estimates.
  • Graphic Packaging Holding Co (NYSE:GPK) shares were also up, gaining 19% to $11.10 after the company reported better-than-expected quarterly financial results.

Equities Trading DOWN

  • Stevanato Group SpA (NYSE:STVN) shares dipped 24% to $14.99 after reporting third-quarter results.
  • Shares of Bioventus Inc (NASDAQ:BVS) were down 20% to $10.56 after the company reported mixed third-quarter financial results and cut its FY26 sales guidance below estimates.
  • Adeia Inc (NASDAQ:ADEA) was down, falling 15% to $17.64 after the company reported worse-than-expected third-quarter financial results and cut its FY26 guidance.

Commodities 

In commodity news, oil traded down 0.6% to $95.90 while gold traded down 0.8% at $3,937.80.

Silver traded down 2.3% to $49.730 on Tuesday, while copper fell 2.6% to $6.4000.

Euro zone

European shares were lower today. The eurozone’s STOXX 600 declined 0.6%, while Spain’s IBEX 35 Index fell 0.8%, London’s FTSE 100 fell 1.1%, Germany’s DAX declined 0.5%, while France’s CAC 40 slipped 0.3%.

Asia Pacific Markets

Asian markets closed mixed on Tuesday, with Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index gaining 0.57%, China’s SSE Composite Index falling 0.82% and India’s BSE Sensex gaining 1.62%.

Economics

  • The RealClearMarkets/TIPP Economic Optimism Index climbed to 48.5 in November from 46.8 in the prior month.
  • The US Logistics Managers’ Index rose to 70.7 in October from 70.2 in the previous month.
  • U.S. factory orders rose 1.8% month-over-month in September compared to a revised 0.3% gain in August.
  • U.S. job openings surged by 333,000 to 7.523 million in September, from a revised 7.19 million in August.

headline: Nasdaq Jumps Over 200 Points as Chip Stocks Gain: Fear & Greed Index Remains in ‘Extreme Fear’ Zone
summary: Markets closed mixed as CNN Fear & Greed stayed at 19 (Extreme Fear); Nasdaq rose 0.83%, Dow fell, Apple dropped and Aehr surged 26%.
content_html:
The CNN Money Fear and Greed Index showed no change in overall market sentiment, while the index remained in the “Extreme Fear” zone on Tuesday.

U.S. stocks settled mixed on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining more than 200 points during the session amid a rebound in chip stocks.

Shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) fell around 2% on Tuesday after the company announced that its gross margin would land between 45% and 46% in the December quarter. That’s below the 46.3% analysts expected, mainly because of higher memory costs.

Pfizer Inc. (NYSE:PFE) on Tuesday reported upbeat results for the third quarter. Shares of Aehr Test Systems (NASDAQ:AEHR) jumped over 26% after the company reported better-than-expected first-quarter financial results and raised its FY27 sales guidance above estimates.

Treasury yields climbed after the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported 7.5 million job openings for September, topping expectations of 7.1 million ahead of the midterm elections. Factory orders increased 1.8% in September, beating the 1.2% forecast after a 0.3% gain in August.

Most sectors on the S&P 500 closed on a negative note, with consumer staples, materials and energy stocks recording the biggest losses on Tuesday. However, industrials and information technology stocks were among the top performers.

The Dow Jones closed lower by around 197 points to 51,786.72 on Tuesday. The S&P 500 rose 0.36% to 7,568.92, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 0.83% at 25,372.01 during Tuesday’s session.

Investors are awaiting earnings results from McDonald’s Corp (NYSE:MCD), Uber Technologies Inc (NYSE:UBER) and Qualcomm Inc (NASDAQ:QCOM) today.

What is CNN Business Fear & Greed Index?

At a current reading of 19, the index remained in the “Extreme Fear” zone on Tuesday, versus a prior reading of 19.

The Fear & Greed Index is a measure of the current market sentiment. It is based on the premise that higher fear exerts pressure on stock prices, while higher greed has the opposite effect. The index is calculated based on seven equal-weighted indicators. The index ranges from 0 to 100, where 0 represents maximum fear and 100 signals maximum greed.

headline: Amazon, Pfizer, Eaton And A Financial Stock On CNBC’s ‘Final Trades’

content_html:
On CNBC’s “Halftime Report Final Trades,” Joshua Brown, co-founder and CEO of Ritholtz Wealth Management, picked Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN).

headline: United Therapeutics Announces $525 Million Royalty Buydown with Pfizer Subsidiary Arena Pharmaceuticals
summary: United Therapeutics has entered into an agreement with Pfizer subsidiary Arena Pharmaceuticals to eliminate royalty obligations for the drug ralinepag in exchange for a $525 million payment.
content_html: United Therapeutics Corporation has amended its exclusive license agreement with Arena Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a subsidiary of Pfizer Inc., regarding the drug ralinepag. The transaction reflects United Therapeutics' confidence in the revenue potential of the ralinepag program.

headline: Pfizer CEO Outlines Strategy for Obesity Drug Market Entry
summary: CEO Albert Bourla detailed Pfizer's strategic approach to the obesity drug market, focusing on the development of berobenatide following the acquisition of Metsera.
content_html: In an interview, Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla discussed the company's strategy to enter the competitive obesity drug market, aiming to challenge established leaders like Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk. The strategy centers on the development of berobenatide, an asset acquired through the $10 billion purchase of Metsera in late 2025. Pfizer is prioritizing differentiated dosing regimens, including a potential once-monthly injection, to gain a competitive edge. While the company is currently progressing through late-stage trials, management does not expect a significant growth inflection from these efforts until 2029.

headline: Pfizer Canada Celebrates 30-Year Partnership with Canadian Paralympic Committee
summary: Pfizer Canada marked three decades of partnership with the Canadian Paralympic Committee by naming its headquarters auditorium the "Paralympic Auditorium" and unveiling a commemorative memorabilia wall.
content_html: Pfizer Canada has commemorated its 30-year partnership with the Canadian Paralympic Committee (CPC) by officially renaming its headquarters auditorium in Kirkland, Quebec, to the "Paralympic Auditorium." The company also unveiled a permanent memorabilia wall to honor the athletes, milestones, and moments that have defined the Paralympic Movement in Canada. Pfizer Canada is recognized as the longest-standing corporate partner of the Paralympic Movement globally. The event was attended by Paralympians, CPC representatives, and community partners to celebrate the long-term commitment to inclusion and Para sport.
